newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges battle against "grey" corruption.
newsitem.headline: China urges battle against "grey" corruption.

text.p: China on Monday called for a battle against "grey corruption", warning Communist Party officials not to become so fond of banquets and business trips that they forget their duty to the people.

"Grey corruption" included activities such as trying to buy official favour with small gifts or lower-ranking officials accompanying leaders to banquets and on sightseeing trips, a commentary in the official People's Daily said.

Such practices, while not as serious as the embezzlement and bribery of "black corruption", had harmed the ruling Communist Party because some members were more keen on seeking personal advancement than on serving the masses, the newspaper said.
"Some believe that power is a magic wand... and some are enthusiastic about wining, dining, amusement and ribbon-cutting ceremonies, forgetting their work and the sufferings of the people."
The paper said it would be easy for such an attitude to lead to worse kinds of corruption, and Beijing should step up its anti-graft efforts to prevent the spread of grey corruption.
"We must strengthen the legal system and gradually expand punishment of 'black corruption' to punishment of 'grey corruption'," it said.
The Communist Party, fearing that popular discontent over rising official graft could loosen its grip on power, has launched several drives to fight corruption in recent years.
